h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ג׳ Pesach — Maamar Gimmel

p: וַאֲפִילּוּ כּוּלָּנוּ חֲכָמִים, כּוּלָּנוּ נְבוֹנִים, כּוּלָּנוּ זְקֵנִים, כּוּלָּנוּ יוֹדְעִים אֶת הַתּוֹרָה.
"And even if we were all wise, all understanding, all elders, all knowing the Torah."
אוֹמְרִים שָׁלֹשׁ לְשׁוֹנוֹת: חֲכָמִים, נְבוֹנִים, יוֹדְעִים, נֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת: חָכְמָה בִּינָה דַּעַת;
It states three terms—"wise," "understanding," "knowing"—corresponding to the three attributes Chochmah, Binah, Da'as;
כּוּלָּנוּ זְקֵנִים — דְּזָקֵן זֶה שֶׁקָּנָה חָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּקִידּוּשִׁין
"all elders"—for an elder (zakein) is "one who has acquired wisdom," as they said in Kiddushin
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁקָּנָה הַחָכְמָה בְּקִנְיָן,
meaning that he acquired wisdom as a permanent acquisition,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הַדַּעַת הַמְּחַבֵּר מוֹחָא וְלִיבָּא, חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, פְּנִימִיּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
which comes through the aspect of Da'as that unites mind and heart—Chochmah and Binah—being the inwardness of Kesser Elyon,
שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה זָקֵן, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
which "zakein" indicates, and as brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' קכ"ט.):
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 129a):
וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן — דְּאָעַל בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִילָּאִין.
"And Avraham was old (zakein)—for he entered into those supernal days."
מִצְוָה עָלֵינוּ לְסַפֵּר בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
"It is a mitzvah upon us to recount the Exodus from Egypt"
וְאֵין הַכַּוָּונָה עַל הַסִּיפּוּר בִּלְבַד, שֶׁעַל זֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ חָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא הַכֹּל דְּבָרִים כְּתוּבִים;
and the intent is not merely the verbal narration, for which wisdom is unnecessary since it is all written down;
רַק הָעִיקַּר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, לְהַכְנִיס הַבְּהִירוּת בַּלֵּב כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם,
rather, the main thing, as we said, is to bring clarity into the heart as though he personally went out of Egypt,
וְשֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ זֶה בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ אָז הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהַחֵירוּת כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ בְּלֵיל זֶה.
and to feel within his soul the joy and freedom just as they felt then when they went out on this night.
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: כָּל הַמַּרְבֶּה לְסַפֵּר בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח
And concerning this they said: "Whoever elaborates in recounting the Exodus from Egypt is praiseworthy"
וְאַף שֶׁהוּא גַּם בִּפְשׁוּטוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁהָיוּ מְסַפְּרִין בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם כָּל אוֹתָהּ הַלַּיְלָה וְכוּלֵּי,
and although it is also meant in its plain sense, as they brought afterward that they recounted the Exodus from Egypt that entire night, etc.,
אֲבָל הָעִיקַּר לְהַכְנִיס בְּהִירוּת הַזֶּה בְּלִבּוֹ,
nevertheless the main thing is to bring this clarity into one's heart,
וְעַל זֶה זָכַר שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁקָּנָה הַחָכְמָה בְּקִנְיָן צָרִיךְ לְעִנְיַן סִיפּוּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
and therefore it mentioned that even one who has acquired wisdom as a permanent possession needs the recounting of the Exodus from Egypt.
וְעַל זֶה הֵבִיא הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And regarding this the holy Zohar brought
בֵּיהּ שַׁעְתָּא כְּנִישׁ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא כָּל פַּמַּלְיָא דִּילֵיהּ וְאָמַר:
"At that hour the Holy One, blessed is He, gathers His entire heavenly retinue and says:
זִילוּ וְשִׁמְעוּ סִיפּוּרָא דְּשִׁבְחָא דִּילִי דְּקָא מִשְׁתָּעוּ בְּנַי וְכוּלֵּי.
'Go and hear the narrative of My praise that My children are recounting, etc.'"
וּמַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הַשֶּׁבַח הַזֶּה שֶׁמִּתְפָּאֵר בּוֹ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ?
And what is so unique about this praise in which Hashem, may He be blessed, glories?
רַק עִיקַּר הַשִּׂמְחָה שֶׁמַּרְגִּישׁ הָאָדָם בְּסִיפּוּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם.
It is precisely the core joy that a person feels in recounting the Exodus from Egypt as though he personally went out of Egypt.
וְזֶה הַסִּיפּוּר הוּא אַחַר שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת וּבָאוּ לִכְלַל שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת.
And this recounting takes place after they emerged from the seven lower attributes and entered into the realm of the first three Sefiros.
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ בְּמַכַּת אַרְבֶּה:
And so we find at the Plague of Locusts:
וּלְמַעַן תְּסַפֵּר בְּאָזְנֵי בִנְךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
"And in order that you may recount in the ears of your son, etc."
וְלָמָּה נִצְרַךְ הַסִּיפּוּר?
And why was the recounting needed then?
דִּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁהָעֶשֶׂר מַכּוֹת הָיוּ כְּנֶגֶד עֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת,
For we have already explained that the ten plagues corresponded to the ten attributes,
שֶׁיֵּשׁ כְּנֶגְדָּן בְּזֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה עֶשֶׂר כִּתְרִין דִּמְסָאֲבוּתָא,
opposite which stand, one corresponding to the other, ten crowns of impurity,
וּבְכָל מִדָּה הָיָה נָגוֹף לְמִצְרַיִם וְרָפוֹא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
and in each attribute there was smiting for Egypt and healing for Israel,
שֶׁהוֹצִיאָם מִקְּלִיפָּה אַחַת וְהִכְנִיסָם לְמִדָּה אַחַת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה;
whereby He brought them out of one husk and brought them into one attribute of holiness;

וְלָכֵן בְּמַכַּת אַרְבֶּה שֶׁהָיָה מַכָּה שְׁמִינִית, וּכְבָר נִתְבָּרְרוּ וְיָצְאוּ מִשֶּׁבַע הַקְּלִיפּוֹת וְנִכְנְסוּ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָּא בְּכָל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה,

therefore, at the Plague of Locusts, which was the eighth plague—when they had already been refined and emerged from the seven husks and entered into holiness from below to above in all seven lower attributes of holiness
כָּתוּב אַחַר זֶה: וּלְמַעַן תְּסַפֵּר בְּאָזְנֵי בִנְךָ וְגוֹמֵר.
it is written after that: "And in order that you may recount in the ears of your son, etc."
וְלָכֵן זָכַר כָּאן גַּם כֵּן כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת: חֲכָמִים, נְבוֹנִים, וְיוֹדְעִים,
And therefore here too it mentioned corresponding to the first three Sefiros: "wise, understanding, and knowing,"
וְזָכַר זְקֵנִים שֶׁחִיבֵּר הַדַּעַת עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמּוֹפִיעַ מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן וְכָאָמוּר.
and it mentioned "elders," who unified Da'as through the illumination from Kesser Elyon, as stated.
וְכֵן נִזְכַּר בְּמַצָּה: עַל שׁוּם וְכוּלֵּי עַד שֶׁנִּגְלָה עֲלֵיהֶם מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
And similarly regarding matzah it is mentioned: "Because, etc., until the King of kings of kings revealed Himself to them"
מְלָכִים הַיְינוּ מַלְכוּת, מַלְכֵי הַיְינוּ שֵׁשׁ מִדּוֹת, מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַיְינוּ שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת,
"kings" is Malchus, "kings of" is the six attributes, and "King of kings of kings" is the first three Sefiros
וְהוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁעוֹנִין עָלָיו דְּבָרִים הַרְבֵּה לְסַפֵּר בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וְכָאָמוּר.
and it is "bread over which many things are answered" to recount the Exodus from Egypt, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Amalah shel Torah 1 — “‘Whoever elaborates in recounting the Exodus is praiseworthy’ implies that one must innovate something about the Exodus, for apart from that we know of the story itself only what is written in the Torah and received from the Sages. So the praiseworthy elaborator is one who can innovate and add praises to the Omnipresent for the good He did us at the Exodus, beyond what is told and known. Before this, speech was in exile; whoever merits to grasp the light of the Exodus, the going out of speech from exile each year at that time, may multiply words as he wishes.” Connection: The same point that the telling cannot mean only repeating what is written; here what is added is one's own new praises, made possible by the yearly release of speech from exile.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shlomo of Radomsk, Tiferes Shlomo, Pesach — “‘Even if we were all wise, all understanding, all elders, all knowing the Torah, it is a mitzvah upon us to recount the Exodus.’ Here they alluded by these words to Chochmah, Binah and Da'as, and to all the Torah and mitzvos; in all of them was the miracle of the Exodus. For in exile all of a person's wisdom, understanding and knowledge are in exile under the hands of strangers; and a person's speech too is in exile, so that he cannot bring his speech out in holiness from potential to actual as he intends. This is the mitzvah of recounting the Exodus on this night: that his speech too goes out of exile.” Connection: The Tiferes Shlomo also reads the three terms as Chochmah, Binah and Da'as and explains why even the wise must recount; he adds that the faculties of mind and speech are themselves in exile and go out on this night through the telling.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 2 — “He said ‘that I may set these signs of Mine in his midst,’ hinting to him the plague of locusts, which corresponds to Binah, the heart, and that is ‘in his midst’; and so it is hinted in ‘and that you may recount in the ears of your son.’ As I heard from my master, the children are the depths of the father's heart. Through the locusts they would merit the attribute of Binah, the heart, and merit the fixing of holiness for generations.” Connection: The same reading of “that you may recount” at the locusts as the stage of the upper attributes; Bo 2 adds that the son is the depths of the father's heart, so the telling fixes holiness for generations.
